findings.current: The entrance had been blown wide open, broad enough for two carriages to pass through side by side, yet not one of the fifty-odd mounted bandits of the Red Wind Band dared set foot inside.
findings.defect: “Blown wide open” adds an explosive mechanism absent from the source, which only describes the entrance as gaping open.
findings.rationale: 뻥 뚫린 describes a wide, unobstructed opening; it does not establish that an explosion created it.
findings.replacement: The entrance gaped wide enough for two carriages to pass through side by side, yet not one of the fifty-odd mounted bandits of the Red Wind Band dared set foot inside.
findings.source: 뻥 뚫린 입구는 마차 두 대가 지나가고도 남을 만큼 넓었지만 오십여 명의 적풍단은 아무도 발을 내딛지 못했다.

findings.current: Some had died with their heads blown apart. Others had been pierced through the abdomen or had their limbs twisted out of shape.
findings.defect: The draft changes broken limbs into limbs merely twisted out of shape, altering the stated fatal injury.
findings.rationale: 사지가 꺾여서 죽었다 explicitly says they died after their limbs were broken.
findings.replacement: Some had died with their heads blown apart. Others had been pierced through the abdomen or killed when their limbs were broken.
findings.source: 머리가 터져 죽고, 복부를 뚫려 죽고, 사지가 꺾여서 죽었다.

findings.current: No one had properly seen when or how Cheol Mubaek's fists moved.
findings.defect: The plural “fists” loses the source's focus on Cheol Mubaek's singular fist or punch.
findings.rationale: 일권 is explicitly singular and reinforces the speed and force of his individual strikes.
findings.replacement: No one had properly seen when or how Cheol Mubaek’s fist moved.
findings.source: 철무백의 일권(一拳)이 언제, 어떻게 움직였는지 제대로 본 사람은 없었다.

findings.current: “Conversation? If you hadn’t betrayed us, Cheonbaek might have lived.”
findings.defect: The draft uses an unestablished partial romanization and omits Cheol Mubaek's affectionate reference to Lee Cheonbaek as his friend.
findings.rationale: 천백 refers to the established Lee Cheonbaek, while 그 친구 explicitly conveys Cheol Mubaek's personal bond with him.
findings.replacement: “Conversation? If you hadn’t betrayed us, Lee Cheonbaek, my friend, might have lived.”
findings.source: “대화? 네가 배신하지 않았더라면 천백, 그 친구는 살 수도 있었다.”

findings.defect: The draft reverses the accusation: it implies Pung Yang did something further because killing Seogwang was insufficient, whereas Cheol Mubaek asks whether he killed Seogwang too, on top of his betrayal.
findings.rationale: 그것으로 부족해서 establishes the prior betrayal as insufficient, and 소광이마저 marks Lee Seogwang as an additional victim.
findings.replacement: “As if that weren’t enough, you killed Lee Seogwang too?”

findings.current: “I’m not generous enough to spare some brat who attacked without knowing his place.”
findings.defect: “Generous” changes Pung Yang's characterization; the source says he is not mild or softhearted enough to spare the brat.
findings.rationale: 유한 성격 refers to a gentle or yielding temperament, not generosity.
findings.replacement: “I’m not softhearted enough to spare a brat who came at me without knowing his place.”
findings.source: “주제도 모르고 덤비는 어린놈을 살려 줄 만큼 유한 성격도 아니고.”

findings.current: “Let’s avenge the Senior Brothers who died at their hands!”
findings.defect: “Senior Brothers” narrows 사형제 to higher-ranking disciples only, losing the broader group of martial brothers across seniority levels.
findings.rationale: 사형제들 collectively denotes fellow male disciples, not only senior brothers.
findings.replacement: “Let’s avenge the martial brothers they killed!”

findings.current: Unlike them, the martial artists of the Mount Heng Sword Sect charged with eyes blazing.
findings.defect: “Eyes blazing” makes the defenders sound conventionally heroic and omits the wild-eyed, nearly frenzied state conveyed by 눈이 뒤집혀.
findings.rationale: 눈이 뒤집혀 depicts a desperate, frenzied charge and is a meaningful characterization cue.
findings.replacement: In stark contrast, the martial artists of the Mount Heng Sword Sect charged at them wild-eyed.
findings.source: 그들은 자신들과는 반대로 눈이 뒤집혀 달려드는 항산검문 무인들의 파죽지세에 속수무책으로 썰려 나갔다.

findings.current: “Any of you who retreat will die by my hand!”
findings.defect: The draft sanitizes the deliberately coarse threat expressed by 놈들 and 뒈질.
findings.rationale: The squad leader uses openly contemptuous, vulgar language to terrorize his subordinates back into line.
findings.replacement: “Any bastard who retreats dies by my hand!”
findings.source: “물러서는 놈들은 내 손에 뒈질 줄 알아!”

findings.current: When more than twenty mounted bandits raised their shields and charged toward the watchtower, desperate shouts rang out.
findings.defect: “More than twenty” turns an approximate quantity into a strict lower bound.
findings.rationale: 이십여 명 means approximately twenty people, not necessarily more than twenty.
findings.replacement: When about twenty mounted bandits raised their shields and charged toward the watchtower, desperate shouts rang out.
findings.source: 이십여 명의 마적들이 방패를 세우고 망루로 돌격해 오자 다급한 외침이 터져 나왔다.

findings.current: The reason the hunter Cheol Mubaek had been able to become the Tiger of Mount Heng was that he had encountered a fortuitous encounter.
findings.defect: “Encountered a fortuitous encounter” is an unnatural repetition.
findings.rationale: This preserves the established rendering of 기연 while producing natural English.
findings.replacement: The hunter Cheol Mubaek became the Tiger of Mount Heng because of a fortuitous encounter.
findings.source: 사냥꾼 철무백이 항산의 호랑이가 될 수 있었던 이유는 기연(奇緣)을 만났기 때문이다.

findings.current:
A ruined house was waiting for him.

So were the bodies of his wife and child.
findings.defect: The draft adds the physical presence of his wife’s and child’s bodies, which the source does not state.
findings.rationale: The source reveals that they died but deliberately does not say that Cheol Mubaek found their bodies there.
findings.replacement: What awaited him was his home in ruins—and the deaths of his wife and child.
findings.source: 자그마치 삼 년 만에 맨손으로 절벽을 기어올라 마을로 돌아간 그를 기다리고 있던 것은 폐허가 된 집, 그리고 아내와 자식의 죽음이었다.

findings.current: By the time he came to his senses, he had already beaten the village’s wealthy landowner and all his servants to death.
findings.defect: “Wealthy landowner” weakens the landowner's scale and local hierarchy; 대지주 denotes a major or leading landowner.
findings.rationale: 대지주 identifies the man by his dominant landholding status, not merely by personal wealth.
findings.replacement: By the time he came to his senses, he had already beaten the village’s leading landowner and all his servants to death.
findings.source: 정신을 차렸을 때는 이미 마을의 대지주와 그의 하인들을 모두 때려죽인 후였다.

findings.current: “Do the Red Wind Band kids not even have a retirement age? Taking up banditry at this old man’s age…”
findings.defect: The second sentence is an ambiguous fragment that can sound as though the speaker is referring to his own age, blunting the joke aimed at Cheol Mubaek.
findings.rationale: 웬 노인네까지 마적질을 mocks the apparent presence of an elderly mounted bandit and sets up Jin Taekyung's immediate embarrassment.
findings.replacement: “Doesn’t the Red Wind Band have a retirement age? Why is an old geezer still out here playing bandit…?”
findings.source: “적풍단 애들은 정년도 없나. 웬 노인네까지 마적질을.”

findings.current: “I’m the one who made the mistake as squad leader, so why am I the one…”
findings.defect: The draft reverses the subject and responsibility: Mujin says the squad leader made the mistake, not that he himself made it while serving as squad leader.
findings.rationale: 조장이 했는데 explicitly assigns the mistake to the squad leader, while 왜 제가 protests being told to apologize for it.
findings.replacement: “The squad leader is the one who made the mistake, so why should I…?”

summary: The draft contains several scene-fact and subject reversals, including an unsupported explosive breach, a mistranslated accusation about Lee Seogwang, an added discovery of bodies, an altered bandit count, and a reversed speaker responsibility in the final exchange. It also loses some hierarchy, characterization, and register.
